\section{Reproducibility and claim status}
\label{app:reproducibility}

\subsection{Logical status of the artifacts}

The theorem depends on the cubical incidence argument,
Proposition~\ref{prop:conditional-law}, Varadhan's heat-kernel asymptotic, the
compact Laplace lemma, and the metric barycenter identity.  No floating-point
value, numerical quadrature, or sampled optimization enters a proof.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.24\textwidth}p{0.18\textwidth}p{0.48\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
Claim & Status & Location \\
\midrule
Private opposite-link realization & proved &
Lemma~\ref{lem:private-opposites} and Proposition~\ref{prop:central-surjectivity} \\
Conditional heat-kernel density & proved & Proposition~\ref{prop:conditional-law} \\
Metric minimizing set and rate & proved &
Lemma~\ref{lem:metric-barycenter} and Theorem~\ref{thm:central-obstruction} \\
Positive-measure stability & proved & Theorem~\ref{thm:open-stability} \\
Dobrushin row-sum failure & proved & Theorem~\ref{thm:dobrushin-failure} \\
Finite incidence ranks for $2\leq d\leq6$ & exact computation &
\texttt{supplement/incidence\_certificate.json} \\
Continuum Yang--Mills existence or mass gap & not claimed &
Section~\ref{sec:scope} \\
Viability of a weighted contour replacement & open & Section~\ref{sec:scope} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{Independent finite check}

From the manuscript root, run
\begin{verbatim}
python3 supplement/verify_incidence.py \
  --output supplement/incidence_certificate.json
python3 -m unittest -v supplement/test_verify_incidence.py
\end{verbatim}
The verifier uses only the Python standard library.  It reports counts,
incident degrees, exact $\mathbb F_2$ ranks, identity-minor tests, and
permutation checks.  The JSON file includes its schema version and the SHA-256
hash of the verifier source.  The manuscript build and visual checks are
described in the accompanying \texttt{README.md} and machine-readable
\texttt{build/build\_report.json}.

\subsection{Data and code statement}

No external dataset was used.  The literature search ledger records queries
and screening decisions as of 21 July 2026.  All code distributed with the
paper is an independently reproducible finite check; it is not a substitute
for an analytic proof.
